title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation  [ the process of becoming like Jesus] part 15
devotional:
I wonder will we make it?

Author, former Desiring God contributor, former Philosophy professor at Moody Bible Institute. (2015—2017), and Trinity Evangelical Divinity PhD. grad Paul Maxwell announced on Instagram, that he is “not a Christian any more.”

I wonder will we make it?

Hillsong songwriter Marty Sampson wrote: “Time for some real talk… I’m genuinely losing my faith… Christians can be the most judgmental people on the planet – they can also be some of the most beautiful and loving people… but it’s not for me. I am not in any more.”

I wonder will we make it?

Dave Gass, the former pastor at Grace Family Fellowship, pastor at Covenant Church and Cedar Community Church, took to social media and announced: “After 40 years of being a devout follower, 20 of those being an evangelical pastor, I am walking away from the faith. Even though this has been a massive bomb dropped in my life, it has been decades in the making.”

I don’t know you but when I hear of people who were once used by God, leaving their faith and stopping following Jesus, I have two main emotions. I feel very sad. I have a friend who was a great bible teacher, and God used him all over the world, now he is very far from God.

The second emotion I feel is fear, fear of not ending the race well. I often wonder, will I be faithful to the end? Will I remain faithful by growing in faithfulness? Or will I end with a cold tired heart that has forgotten how to be passionate about Jesus?

How we cross the line is more important than how we started. We have no control as to when we will cross the finishing line, but we are absolutely responsible for how we cross it so let us look at some verses that will help us finish well:- In Galatians 6:6-10 Paul wrote these words ‘Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word should share all good things with their instructor. 7 Do not be deceived: God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows. 8 Whoever sows to please their flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; whoever sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life. 9 Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up. 10 Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.’

Paul gives us five areas of relationships where we need to be intentional, where we need to work hard at sowing that which will produce a harvest of eternal life. Before we look at this we need to first consider the principle of sowing and reaping.

Madame Chiang Kai-shek once wrote: "If the past has taught us anything it is that every cause brings its effect, every action has a consequence. We Chinese have a saying: "If a man plants melons he will reap melons; if he sows beans, he will reap beans." And this is true of everyone's life; good begets good, and evil leads to evil. True enough, the sun shines on the saint and the sinner alike, and too often it seems that the wicked prosper. But we can say with certainty that, with the individual as with the nation, the flourishing of the wicked is an illusion, for, unceasingly, life keeps books on us all. In the end, we are all the sum total of our actions. Character cannot be counterfeited, nor can it put on and cast off as if it were a garment to meet the whim of the moment. Like the markings on wood which are ingrained in the very heart of the tree, character requires time and nurturing for growth and development. Thus also, day by day, we write our own destiny; for inexorably...we become what we do." ccel.org. Accessed 04/08/25

Let me try and explain the implications of this principle.

[a] A harvest may be sown in secret but the harvest itself cannot be hidden.

This is so important. The seeds we sow in private will eventually become evident. In some ways the people we are and the things we do when nobody but God sees us, is when we sow prominent seeds that will have a massive influence on who we will become in the future.

[b] We alone are responsible for the seed we sow. Nobody else can sow our seed. Your seeds are your seeds, we cannot hold other people responsible for the people we become. Do others influence and affect us? Yes. But no matter how I have been treated or mistreated by others, the harvest I will reap and the character I become is due to the seeds I am/have sowed.

[c] Time might pass before the harvest ripens but it will come.

The harvest will take time, be it a good harvest or a bad harvest it will come, That is both good news and bad news. I have been with people who have sown good seed and as they were dying there was a dignified composure about them. Conversely, others who have planted poor/bad seed all their lives have been bitter and agitated as they have faced death.

[d] The nature of the seed we sow will determine the harvest.

If we sow good seed like love, mercy, compassion, kindness and the like, we can expect a good harvest. That is sowing to the Spirit. However, if we are sowing seed that is consistent with our sinful nature then we should expect to develop a character that is inconsistent with the image and purposes of God.

[d] The harvest will always be greater/more than the seed that you sow. The seeds we sow may seem to be small, like attitudes, thoughts, perceptions, prestiges. Seeds are almost inconsequential, they are so small, however, the size of the seed will not determine the size of the plant it will produce.

[e] You can do nothing about your past harvests but you can about future harvests. The harvest we reaped in the future does not have to be the same as the harvest we have reaped in the past. We can easily think, ‘if my circumstances are different in the future then I will be a better/happier person. The problem is, our circumstances do not determine the harvest we will reap in our characters. We can move homes, change our jobs, get married, but if we are sowing the seeds you have always sown, then nothing in you is going to change.

[g] The sowing and reaping principle applies to every area of our lives. When we sow seed we sow it in every single area of our lives, there is nothing in our lives immune from the sowing and reaping principle.

‘I wonder will we make it?’
prayer: Father help me be intentional in sowing good seed.
